source_fields.formulation: Each round draws a fresh random parameter vector, and the learner observes only its exact projection along the selected action. Actions lie in the unit p-norm ball. Noise variance depends jointly on the direction and the public covariance matrix.
source_fields.solution_goal: Minimize performance as defined by the metric, guarantee, and native resource.

source_fields.instance: $$\mathcal A=\{a\in\mathbb R^d:\|a\|_p\le1\},\qquad 1<p\le2,\qquad q=\frac{p}{p-1}.$$ $$\theta_t\overset{\mathrm{i.i.d.}}\sim\nu,\qquad \mathbb E\theta_t=\theta_*,\qquad \operatorname{Cov}(\theta_t)=\Sigma,\qquad |\langle a,\theta_t\rangle|\le1\quad\text{almost surely, for every }a\in\mathcal A.$$ Randomness comes from a fresh parameter vector each round; the feedback is not a linear regression observation with additive homoscedastic scalar noise. $$N=T,\qquad \sigma_q^2=\left(\sum_{i=1}^{d}\Sigma_{ii}^{q/2}\right)^{2/q}.$$ Here $N$ counts scalar observations. The quantity $\sigma_q^2$ is defined by the covariance diagonal and cannot be replaced by the maximum action variance.

source_fields.parameter_domain_description: T: $T\in\mathbb N,\ T\ge1$ (public); d: $d\in\mathbb N,\ d\ge1$ (public); \delta_{\mathrm{conf}}: $0<\delta_{\mathrm{conf}}<1$ (public); p: $1<p\le2$ (public); q: $q=p/(p-1)\in[2,\infty)$ (public); \Sigma: $\Sigma\in\mathbb R^{d\times d},\ \Sigma\succeq0$ (public); \sigma_q^2: $\sigma_q^2\ge0$ (public)

operations.query_signature: $$Y_t=\langle a_t,\theta_t\rangle,\qquad \operatorname{Var}(Y_t\mid a_t)=a_t^{\mathsf T}\Sigma a_t.$$ Choose $a_t$ first, then draw a fresh $\theta_t$ and reveal only the scalar projection. The same $\theta_t$ defines all counterfactual rewards that round, but other projections are hidden. Causal policies are allowed. Inputs $d,p,q,T,\delta_{\mathrm{conf}}$ and covariance $\Sigma$ are public; the distribution $\nu$ and mean $\theta_*$ are hidden. Received feedback may be stored and reused computationally; no unrevealed historical information or extra queries to exhausted samples are available. Within-round exceptions require explicit full-function or common-sample access.

source_fields.feasibility: The output is the complete action trajectory satisfying feasibility and timing requirements. Randomized mixtures may be implemented before acting. Retrospective averages or convex combinations cannot replace actions that have already incurred loss. No additional optimal value or certificate is required.
source_fields.allowed_postprocessing: Previously executed online actions cannot be changed.
source_fields.certificate_requirement: No function value, optimality certificate, or final recommendation is required unless explicitly listed for this axis.

source_fields.normalization: Use the cumulative quantity over T rounds without dividing by T. Preserve the displayed order of probability or expectation.
source_fields.finiteness_conditions: The unit mean/loss range or the stated Lipschitz amplitude bound limits the per-round excess loss to two. Cumulative regret is therefore at most 2T. Unbounded observation noise does not enter pseudo-regret.

source_fields.complete_expression: For every $\nu$ satisfying the stated support constraint, static pseudo-regret is controlled with probability at least $1-\delta_{\mathrm{conf}}$. This notation results from setting the source failure parameter to $\delta_{\mathrm{conf}}/2$.
